text.p: These are the leading stories in the Zimbabwe press on Thursday.
Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- The government has advised suspended Zimbabwe Newspapers Group chief executive Simba Makoni to resign, but he has allegedly refused to comply, preferring to be sacked.
- After several months of promises, the government is expected to announce a new tariff structure on February 14, official sources said.

- Top Zimbabwean civil servants and some politicians owe the public construction and national housing ministry Z$40 million in default payments for private houses built for them using public funds, sources said.
- Harare city council's procedure board is worried that most council tenders are being won by large companies and is now pressing for an urgent review of tender regulations and standing resolutions.

- A recent survey has shown that most Zimbabwean companies are paying huge salaries which do not reflect workers' productivity, a situation which could have triggered the collapse of some of the firms.

- The localisation process of regional conglomerate, Trans Zambezi Industries, which will see the transfer to Zimbabwe of Z$150 million worth of shares to be offered to Art Corporation and Chloride shareholders, will create an eight percent local ownership in the group.

- The visiting president of the Coca-Cola Company, Douglas Ivester, on Wednesday announced a Z$600 million investment programme designed to double the company's business in Zimbabwe and create thousands of jobs in downstream industries over the next four years.

- Coca Cola's Ivester said his group was fully behind the Zimbabwean government's drive to economically empower the country's majority blacks and would make its contribution by assisting entrepreneurs at the retail level.
